from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We divide the population into three compartments.",
            "Susceptible: those who can still catch it.",
            "Infectious: those currently spreading the virus.",
            "Recovered: those who are now immune.",
            "Nodes transition through these states over time."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Core Components: Defining S, I, and R", lecture_lines)
        
        # Helper to create compartment with icon
        def create_compartment(color, asset_path, label_text):
            node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=color, fill_opacity=0.3)
            icon = SVGMobject(asset_path).set_color(color).scale(0.35)
            label = Text(label_text, font_size=20, color=color)
            label.next_to(node, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            return VGroup(node, icon, label)
        
        # Define compartments
        s_group = create_compartment("#FFFF00", "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg", "S")
        i_group = create_compartment("#FF0000", "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/virus.svg", "I")
        r_group = create_compartment("#00FF00", "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/person.svg", "R")
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(s_group, 'B2', 'B2', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(i_group, 'B3', 'B3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(r_group, 'B4', 'B4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Arrows
        arrow_s_i = Arrow(start=s_group.get_right(), end=i_group.get_left(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        arrow_i_r = Arrow(start=i_group.get_right(), end=r_group.get_left(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(s_group), FadeIn(i_group), FadeIn(r_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Create(arrow_s_i), Create(arrow_i_r))
        equation = MathTex("S + I + R = N", font_size=36)
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'D2', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(equation))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transmission happens when infectious meet susceptible individuals.",
            "Recovery occurs as infectious individuals eventually recover.",
            "Mathematical rates define these transition rules.",
            "Blue dots turn red upon contact.",
            "Red dots slowly transition to green."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Engine: Mathematical Transition Rules", lecture_lines)
        
        # Equations
        eq1 = MathTex(r"dS/dt = -\beta SI/N").set_color("#FFFF00")
        eq2 = MathTex(r"dI/dt = \beta SI/N - \gamma I").set_color("#FF0000")
        eq3 = MathTex(r"dR/dt = \gamma I").set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Assets
        human = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/human.svg")
        microbe = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microbe.svg")
        patient = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/patient.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.place_in_area(eq1, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_in_area(eq2, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.place_in_area(eq3, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        self.place_at_grid(human, 'E2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(microbe, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)

        self.play(human.animate.move_to(microbe.get_center()), run_time=0.5)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The epidemic curve shows virus spread over time.",
            "The peak represents the maximum infectious count.",
            "We can flatten the curve using interventions.",
            "Adjusting parameters shows different outcome scenarios.",
            "Social distancing directly impacts these curves."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Simulation: Visualizing the Curves", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.2],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE},
            x_length=5, y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E4', scale_factor=0.75)
        
        # S, I, R Curves
        s_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.9 * np.exp(-0.5 * x), color=YELLOW)
        i_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x * np.exp(-0.5 * x), color=RED)
        r_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 - 0.9 * np.exp(-0.5 * x) - 0.5 * x * np.exp(-0.5 * x), color=GREEN)
        curves = VGroup(s_curve, i_curve, r_curve)
        self.place_in_area(curves, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("S", color=YELLOW, font_size=24),
            Text("I", color=RED, font_size=24),
            Text("R", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        ).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(labels, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        virus_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/virus.svg")
        virus_icon_2 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/virus.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(s_curve))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(virus_icon, 'C4', scale_factor=0.1)
        self.play(Create(i_curve), FadeIn(virus_icon))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(r_curve))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(virus_icon_2, 'C5', scale_factor=0.1)
        self.play(Indicate(i_curve), FadeIn(virus_icon_2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        flatten_text = Text("Flatten the curve", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(flatten_text, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(flatten_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics
outline.target_audience: University Students (Introductory Data Science or Biology)

sections.title: Hook: The Problem of Prediction
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of predicting how a virus spreads in a population. Define the necessity of modeling to inform public health decisions.
sections.example: A single sneeze in a crowded subway car—how does that translate into thousands of cases?

sections.title: Core Components: Defining S, I, and R
sections.content: Break down the three compartments: Susceptible (can catch it), Infectious (has it), and Recovered/Removed (immune or deceased). Use a visual flow diagram of nodes moving from one bucket to another.
sections.example: Representing students as colored dots: Blue (Susceptible), Red (Infectious), and Green (Recovered).

sections.title: The Engine: Mathematical Transition Rules
sections.content: Explain the interaction between S and I (transmission rate β) and I to R (recovery rate γ). Use a graphical representation of two differential equations showing how the slopes of the curves interact.
sections.example: An animation showing Red dots bumping into Blue dots turning them Red, while Red dots slowly transition to Green over time.

sections.title: Simulation: Visualizing the Curves
sections.content: Show the classic 'Epidemic Curve.' Explain the 'Peak' and the concept of 'Flattening the Curve' by adjusting the parameters β and γ visually.
sections.example: Comparing a 'High Peak' scenario (uncontrolled) vs. a 'Flattened Curve' (social distancing/masks) through side-by-side graph animation.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize how simple rules create complex population behavior. Mention limitations of SIR (e.g., population mixing) and encourage further exploration of SEIR models.
sections.example: Using the model to predict herd immunity thresholds for a hypothetical animal population outbreak in a nature reserve.
